header:
Date: 2025-04-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (LuminaHealth CTO), Anika (ML Platform), Ben (SRE), Claire (PM)
Topic: weekly POC sync - model catalog tradeoffs, version pinning, rollback tabletop
summary: Quick sync to review latest evals from the pilot, reconcile catalog choices for latency vs quality, and walk through a tabletop rollback scenario. Action items assigned for benchmarks, prompt set delivery, and a rollback runbook draft. Some transcription glitches on product names (Redwood Private heard as Redwood Privates) and "KV cash" instead of KV cache.
topics: pilot evaluation metrics: p50/p95/p99 and hallucination rates
model catalog tradeoffs: larger model accuracy vs quantized latency
version pinning policy and canary/soft-fallback approach
security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 mention
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45 minutes, quick agenda - benchmarks, catalog choices, and a tabletop rollback.
[00:18] Jordan: sounds good, I just want to make sure the p95 numbers we saw last week were stable, we saw a spike at end of day.
[00:30] Ethan: right, that was the tail when batch sizes hit 8, we think continuous batching and the kv cache - sorry kv cash in the logs - needs a tweak for our long prompts.
[00:52] Anika: side question, how big of a delta do you expect if we pin to a smaller quantized variant? I worry about hallucination uptick.
[01:10] Priya: good call, from our internal runs the quantized 8-bit variant reduces cost by ~35% but the eval showed a 4-6% lift in hallucination on the 'clinical-sum' prompts. It's workload dependent.
[01:35] Ben: that aligns with what we saw in our smoke tests, but latency improves a lot, p95 drops from 720ms to 380ms for short sequences.
[01:52] Claire: for product we care more about user intent correctness than absolute latency below 500ms, so there is tradeoff.
[02:10] Maya: yep, that tradeoff is the core decision. today we want to pick a pinning strategy and walk through rollback triggers.
[02:28] Ethan: quick show of the benchmark summary - we ran three models: Atlas-Open like baseline (note: speaker mislabels model names), Redwood-XL quantized, and Redwood-XS (fast endpoint). p50/p95/p99 and token cost per 1k tokens attached in the sheet I sent.
[02:55] Jordan: can you repeat the p95 for the XL quantized?
[03:05] Ethan: p95 ~ 380ms with batching optimized; cost per 1k tokens about $1.8 on hosted, Dedicated gives about 20% cost improvement but adds commit.
[03:27] Jordan: committed Dedicated is an option if we need sustained throughput, but we also need private deployment for PHI — will that affect rollback options?
[03:45] Maya: good question. Private (VPC) deployments use the same control plane, so rollbacks are still supported but the runbook has an extra step to push config to your VPC cluster. We'll add that detail.
[04:08] Anika: on rollbacks, what are the triggers we recommend? metric-based, manual, or combined?
[04:22] Priya: combined. threshold based for p95/latency and hallucination rate on the prompt set, plus a manual cutoff if product signals too many incorrect replies. We recommend a 24-hour automated rollback window for regressions that cross both thresholds.
[04:45] Ben: define the hallucination metric though, is it classification on golden prompts?
[04:55] Ethan: yes, we measure % of responses failing an exact-match or semantic-check on the golden prompt set; we'll need Lumina's prompts to finalize thresholds.
[05:12] Claire: timeline — if we pick a model this week can we do a canary next Tuesday?
[05:20] Maya: yes, assuming we get prompts and Redwood shares the benchmark logs by Friday.
[05:30] Jordan: let's run a tabletop: scenario — we cut to quantized-XL for cost savings, after 6 hours we see a 3x uptick in hallucinations on the 'patient-summaries' prompt and p95 creeps to 600ms. Walk me through.
[05:58] Priya: first step is detection via the eval webhook; if both hallucination and latency exceed thresholds the system flags an automated soft-fallback to the previous pinned version for 10% traffic. That buys time to validate.
[06:20] Ben: who initiates a full rollback? SE or customer on-call?
[06:28] Maya: default is customer SRE (Ben) approves, notified by Redwood via PagerDuty and in-console action. There's also an auto-cut to full rollback if both thresholds are severe. We'll document the Escalation > Owner chain.
[06:50] Jordan: what's the risk to stateful sessions / KV cache on a rollback?
[06:58] Ethan: KV cache warmup could cause a temporary latency spike; the runbook recommends a controlled ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 15 minutes and warm KV by replaying recent traffic in shadow.
[07:20] Claire: will rolling back change embeddings indexes or downstream rerankers?
[07:28] Priya: not directly, but if model outputs change you'll want to re-eval reranker thresholds; we recommend keeping embeddings stable by pinning embedding model separately.
[07:45] Jordan: embedding stability matters for search recall; ok we'll pin embedding model independent of generator.
[07:58] Maya: note about canaries - Redwood supports shadow traffic and soft fallback rules; we can configure automatic rollback if canary error budget exceeded.
[08:15] Anika: any limitations for Private on-prem? e.g., kernel optimizations or quantization support?
[08:25] Ethan: on-prem supports quantization but kernel parity depends on hardware—some older GPUs won't see the same perf. We'll include a compatibility matrix.
[08:40] Jordan: security stuff — do you have KMS integration for key rotation and audit logs accessible?
[08:48] Maya: yes, KMS / HSM integrations and audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private, SOC2 compliance as well; we'll attach the security package.
[09:02] Ben: we need a short SLA statement for the pilot in case of outages.
[09:10] Maya: we'll draft a pilot SLA bullet list for inclusion in the runbook.
[09:20] Claire: back to model tradeoffs — can we split traffic by route, send sensitive routes to larger model and others to quantized?
[09:33] Priya: yes, routing by intent or route config is straightforward; Redwood routing policies let you send x% to a higher-quality model.
[09:45] Jordan: and that's how we minimize cost while protecting critical flows.
[09:52] Ethan: exactly. Now about pinning policy proposals — three options: 1) strict pin (pin to single version), 2) tiered pin (pin primary, soft fallback to secondary), 3) dynamic pin with auto-swap based on quality signals.
[10:10] Claire: tiered pin seems pragmatic for now.
[10:16] Jordan: agree, tiered pin + manual approval for full rollouts.
[10:24] Maya: we'll outline that in the runbook and include the cutoff thresholds we discussed.
[10:30] Ben: what's the minimum rollback time? how quickly can you flip traffic?
[10:36] Ethan: instant at control plane level but warm-up and KV cache mean effective normalization in ~15 minutes.
[10:44] Anika: for our compliance team we might need an audit trail showing who executed the rollback and why.
[10:52] Maya: Redwood's console logs user actions and records the metric triggers; that will be in the audit logs.
[11:05] Jordan: okay let's get more detail on the benchmark — can we see raw tail latency distribution not just p95?
[11:14] Ethan: yes we'll share histogram CSVs.
[11:20] Claire: also want to see token-level cost on worst-case prompts.
[11:28] Maya: action: Ethan share detailed logs, Maya share cost sheet.
[11:35] Priya: one more thing — consider a 'cost cap' route where once cost per minute crosses X we auto-route to cheaper fallback. Useful if traffic surges.
[11:50] Jordan: ok interesting. We need to avoid noisy auto-routing; must tie to business signal.
[12:00] Ben: for the tabletop, after soft-fallback we validate on golden prompts for 30 minutes; if still failing then full rollback with SRE approval.
[12:12] Maya: we'll phrase that as an automated policy + manual override.
[12:20] Anika: timeline recap?
[12:25] Maya: Redwood provides benchmark + runbook draft by Friday, Lumina provides prompt set by Thursday, then next Tuesday canary.
[12:35] Claire: assign owners on the calendar invite please.
[12:40] Maya: done. Any other questions?
[12:44] Jordan: just one: do we have a way to test the rollback without impacting prod?
[12:50] Ethan: yes, tabletop + a dry-run mode that runs the same orchestration in a staging cluster and validates the steps. We'll help you run it.
[13:05] Maya: great, we'll follow up with links to the dry-run playbook and attach the security pack.
[13:12] (crosstalk) Claire: thanks everyone.
[13:20] End of recording.
